name: Week 27 Pull — Short Day, and the Pull-Up Question Gets Answered (Spotlight: Pull-Ups + Face Pull)
description:
**Warmups are baked into each block's notes as a reminder.**

**This is the short third day.** Chest-supported row, reverse fly and cable crunch come out — one row is enough, the face pull covers the rear delt, and the day needs to fit a window rather than fill one.

**Pull-ups sit two days after push instead of one.** Last time they ran the day after a heavy press day and fell to 8 / 7 / 6 with the last set collapsing to singles. This is the clean read.

**The DB row pyramid is written as 75 / 85 / 95** — the loads you actually ran by accident, which produced the best row datapoint of the block.

**The high cable curl steps up 10 across the board**, which was your call.

dayOverview.theme:
A deliberately short day with one question in it. Last week pull ran twenty-four hours after a heavy push day for the first time, the right shoulder read 'extra crispy,' and the pull-ups dropped from 10 / 8 / 7 / 5 to 8 / 7 / 6 and then singles — on the lift that has improved most in the whole program. This week legs sits between push and pull and the shoulders get a full forty-eight hours. If the pull-ups come back, the adjacency explanation is confirmed and the push → legs → pull order stays permanent.

The face pull takes the second spotlight for a reason that has nothing to do with the gym. Rocking, carrying and long one-armed holds pull the shoulders forward all day now, and pulling work at the back of the shoulder is the highest-value thing in this session for the next few months — not the accessory it looks like on paper.

spotlights.why: The one clean test this week. Same lift, same tempo, same bar — the only variable changed is that push is two days back instead of one. Whatever number comes out is the answer.
The postural load has changed. Hours of rocking, carrying and forward-reaching at crib and car-seat height make rear-shoulder and upper-back pulling the highest-value work in the program right now.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W28 — lat pulldown + chest-supported row when it comes back in. W29 — DB row and incline curl. W30 — pull-ups again once the adjacency question is settled.
watchpoints: 🛑 keep it shy — the cue is the cap: pull-ups, DB row, lat pulldown, incline curl. Grip and position lifts where the honest ceiling is the rep the cue breaks, not the rep the muscle quits.
🔥 near-failure last set OK: face pull, high cable curl. Isolation work where form holds at the limit.

**Right shoulder read 'extra crispy' last week.** Watch it through the warmup and the first pull-up set. If it is still talking, drop to three sets and keep every rep clean rather than pushing the fourth.

**The left side fades before the right on the row.** At 95 the right held ten clean reps and the left lost grip and strength at eight. That is the expected shape — finish the left where it finishes, no straps.
**Band-pull-apart is the pull-day shoulder anchor.** Keep the warmup lean otherwise; this day is short on purpose.

sets.name: Warmup (Pull-up Bar Station)
sets.notes: Band-pull-apart is the pull-day shoulder anchor. Keep the block lean — everything here happens at or near the bar.

exercises.notes: **The shoulder anchor for pull day.** Light band, slow, squeeze the shoulder blades together without shrugging.
Passive hang. **Also your first read on the right shoulder today** — note whether it is quiet.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)
sets.notes: Before anything gets loaded. This is the block that keeps the shoulder quiet through pull day.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair, behind the back, 2 sets.
- Straight up and down, no rolling
- **Squeeze at the top**, slow release
- Neck long throughout

sets.name: 🔆 Pull-Ups — Straight Bar, 4 Sets, 3s Eccentric (Spotlight) 🛑
sets.notes:
**Bodyweight, 4 sets to form failure, 3s eccentric on every rep.** Straight bar, not the swivel handles.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — this is a controlled test, so run it clean:**
- **Two weeks ago, rested: 10 / 8 / 7 / 5** with the tempo intact
- **Last week, one day after push: 8 / 7 / 6, then singles.** Right shoulder crispy, less power than usual
- **This week push is two days back.** Same bar, same tempo, nothing else changed
- **3s eccentric on every rep** — the tempo is what makes the numbers comparable. A faster rep is not the same rep
- **Form failure, not muscular failure.** The set ends when the eccentric stops being 3 seconds or the shoulders shrug up to start the rep
- **Do not chase the old number.** Whatever comes out today is the data; forcing it wrecks the experiment and the shoulder
- **If the right shoulder is still crispy, run three sets** and log that instead

**Reflection:** did the reps come back toward 10 / 8 / 7 / 5? And how did the right shoulder feel on set 1 compared to last week?

exercises.notes:
Bodyweight, 4 sets, **3s eccentric every rep.** Straight bar.
- Set ends when the tempo breaks or the shoulders shrug up
- **Log all four numbers** — this is the week's one real test
- Three sets is a fine answer if the shoulder is talking

sets.name: DB Rack / Bench Block — Incline Curl → DB Row (3 Rounds)
sets.notes:
**Both lifts live at the DB rack and the adjustable benches — take them as one station and do not walk away between them.**

The chest-supported row and the reverse fly come out this week. One row is enough on a short day, and the face pull covers the rear delt.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 25lb, 3 sets of 10 each side.

Best left-arm result yet last time — all sets completed without failing, even with the left reading tired from the push day two days earlier.
- **Bench at 45°, arms hanging fully behind the body** — the stretch at the bottom is the whole reason for the incline
- **Do not swing the shoulder forward** to start the rep
- Slow eccentric, full extension at the bottom

**LOAD: pyramid 75 → 85 → 95.** One set at each, each side.

These are the loads you actually ran, and they produced the best row datapoint of the block: the right side held 10 clean at 95, the left lost grip and strength at 8.
- **Expect the left to finish around 8 on the 95.** That is the honest number — no straps, and the grip is the point
- **Chest supported on the bench**, spine long, no twisting to finish the rep
- **Elbow drives back past the ribs**, not out to the side
- Slow eccentric, full stretch at the bottom
- **Let the reps creep rather than the load** — the left ceiling moved on its own last time

sets.name: Lat Pulldown 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:**
- Regular lat pulldown machine: **160**
- Cable pulley: **70/side (140 total)**
Pick whichever is free; **note which equipment + number you used in the log.**

160 ran clean across all three sets last time and read notably easy after the pull-ups. It holds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** regular machine **160** · cable pulley **70/side**. Log which.
- **Pack the shoulders DOWN before the elbows move** — blades into the back pockets first
- Bar to the collarbones, chest up
- **Slow eccentric** — that is where 160 got difficult before
- Ribs down, no leaning back to finish

sets.name: 🔆 Face Pull — the Most Valuable Lift in This Session Right Now (Spotlight) 🔥
sets.notes:
**LOAD: 62.5, and keep adding as it gets easy.** One station, one ladder — take whichever pulley is free and keep climbing the same line. 3 sets of 20.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — why this one matters more than usual right now:**
- **Your postural load changed this month.** Rocking a baby, carrying a car seat, long one-armed holds and repeated reaching at crib height all pull the shoulders forward and round the upper back
- **This is the direct antidote**, and it is worth more to you over the next few months than any pressing lift in the program
- **Pull to the face, not the chest.** Hands finish beside the ears, elbows high and wide
- **External rotation at the end** — knuckles rotate back, like a double bicep pose. That rotation is the part most people skip and it is the part that matters
- **Squeeze and hold for a beat** at the end position rather than snapping back
- **Traps stay quiet.** If the shoulders ride up toward the ears, drop the pin
- Last set can run near failure — this is safe isolation work

**Reflection:** does the end-range external rotation still feel available on the right side, or does it run out earlier than the left?

exercises.notes:
**LOAD: 62.5+.** One station, one ladder — keep adding as it gets easy. 3 sets of 20.
- **Hands finish beside the ears**, elbows high
- **Rotate the knuckles back** at the end of every rep
- Hold a beat, slow return
- Traps quiet

sets.name: High Cable Curl — Ascending, Up 10 Across the Board 🔥
sets.notes:
**LOAD:**
- Cable column (your 'double column'): **190 → 200 → 210** ascending, one set each
- Single pulley: **62.5**
Pick whichever is free; **note which equipment + number you used in the log.**

The whole ladder moves up 10 — your call after running 180 / 190 / 200 twice and finding it a good pyramid with room. **Single arm.** The top set is the near-failure one, which is what makes the ascending shape self-limiting.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column **190 / 200 / 210** ascending · single pulley **62.5**. Log which.
- **Single arm**, cable high, elbow fixed in space
- **Do not let the elbow drift forward** — the upper arm stays put
- Squeeze at the top, slow return to full extension
- Top set can run near failure

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)
sets.notes: Five minutes, every gym day. Slow breathing throughout.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm, elbow at MID height. Directly undoes the forward-shoulder posture.
Passive. Let the shoulders decompress after the pulling.

tips: The pull-up numbers are the point of the day — log all four sets, whatever they say.
Nothing goes near failure except the face pull and the top curl. This is a short day, not a hard one.
The cool-down stays even when the session gets cut short.
